questions.question: Two Girls Meena and Reena are ranked 7th and 11th, respectively from the top in a class of 41 students. What are their respective ranks from the bottom in the class?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Two Girls Meena and Reena are ranked 7th and 11th, respectively from the top in a class of 41 students. What are their respective ranks from the bottom in the class?
questions.solution:
Rank from the bottom = Total number of students - Rank from the top + 1

Position of Meena from the bottom = 41 - 7 + 1 = 35th

Position of Reena from the bottom = 41 - 11 + 1 = 31th

questions.question: A man sees smoke coming from a building and hears people shouting. What should he do first ?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->A man sees smoke coming from a building and hears people shouting. What should he do first ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Statement :
A man sees smoke coming from a building and hears people shouting.

Option 1 — Run away immediately:
Running away may keep the man safe, but it doesn't help people in danger and could delay professional help. Not the best first action.

Option 2 — Try to enter the building:
Entering a smoke-filled building is dangerous and could put the man at risk, too.

Option 3 — Call emergency services:
This is the correct first action.

Calling the fire department/police/ ambulance gets trained responders on the way, allows professionals to coordinate rescue and containment, and can provide instructions (stay back, evacuate nearby, etc.). 

Option 4 — Ignore and move on:
Clearly inappropriate — people may be in danger.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: If 'I' stands for '+', 'J' stands for '×', 'K' stands for '÷', and 'L' stands for '-', what will come in place of the question mark '?' in the following equation? 38 I (3 J 4) L (16 K 2) I 11 =?
questions.questionHtml:
If 'I' stands for '+', 'J' stands for '×', 'K' stands for '÷', and 'L' stands for '-', what will come in place of the question mark '?' in the following equation?
38 I (3 J 4) L (16 K 2) I 11 =?
questions.solution:
Decoding the given information:

Alphabet I J K L
Meaning + × ÷ -

Now replacing the sign from left to right using BODMAS Rule, we get:

⇒ 38 + (3 × 4) - (16 ÷ 2) + 11 = ?

⇒ 38 + 12 - 8 + 11  ⇒ 61 - 8 = 53.

questions.question: In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements. Statements: I. All P are G. II. Some F are P. Conclusion: I. All G are P. II. All P are F. III. Some F are not G.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

Statements:

I. All P are G.

II. Some F are P.

Conclusion:

I. All G are P.

II. All P are F.

III. Some F are not G.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follows
options.html: Both conclusions II and III follows

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. All P are G.

II. Some F are P.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

Conclusions:

I. All G are P - False (Because, All P are G gives some G are P, but all G are P can be possible only).

II. All P are F - False (Because, Some F are P gives some P are F, but all P are F can be possible only).

III. Some F are not G - False (Because, Some F are definitely G, but no information given about the remaining part, so it can be possible only).

So, Neither conclusion follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Direction : In each of these questions are given two statements (A) and (B) These statements may be either independent causes or may be effects of independent causes or of a common cause. Read both the statements and give an answer. (A): Rohit is a healthy boy. (B): His mother is very particular about the food he eats.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In each of these questions are given two statements (A) and (B) These statements may be either independent causes or may be effects of independent causes or of a common cause. Read both the statements and give an answer.

(A): Rohit is a healthy boy.

(B): His mother is very particular about the food he eats.

options.text: If statement (A) is the cause and statement (B) is its effect.
options.html: If statement (A) is the cause and statement (B) is its effect.

options.text: If statement (B) is the cause and statement (A) is its effect.
options.html: If statement (B) is the cause and statement (A) is its effect.

options.text: If If both statements are effects of independent causes.
options.html: If If both statements are effects of independent causes.

options.text: If both statements are effects of some common cause.
options.html: If both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.solution:
The logic followed is:

Rohit is healthy because of his mother's care.

Thus his mother who is very particular about the foods he eat is the cause and the effect is Rohit is healthy.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Additional Information 

What are Causes?

Causes are the conditions under which an event occurs.

For example, can you guess the causes for the following? 

The police increased security around the President's house.

Lots of people buy a particularly expensive brand of washing machines around Diwali. Easily, we can guess the causes for the above events. 

There were reports of threats against the President. 

There was a high discount or sale for that brand during Diwali.

Sufficient & Necessary Conditions:

In a cause and effect question, the cause is the sufficient condition. It is assumed that the sufficient condition of the occurrence of the events must include the different necessary conditions as well. 

A necessary condition is one that must be satisfied for the occurrence of an event. 

E.g. You must adhere to the deadline to get your work appraised. 

This means if you get your work appraised, you have to adhere to the deadline. Or; if you do not adhere to the deadline, you do not get your work appraised. 

A condition is called a sufficient condition if in a certain event, you are satisfied with the results.

E.g. Being human is a sufficient condition for being a mammal. The act of being a human is not possible unless one is also a mammal. But it is not necessary that being human is a necessary condition for being a mammal.

questions.question: Directions : Statement is given followed by two inferences I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given inferences, if any, follow from the given statement. Statement : Dakhni inscriptions are rare, and the one at the Bijapur dargah is the oldest surviving inscription in the language that needs to be taken care of by the government. Inferences : I: The government will introduce new plans for preserving the Dakhni inscriptions at Bijapur dargah. II: Dakhni is a newly emerging language.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Statement is given followed by two inferences I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given inferences, if any, follow from the given statement.

Statement: Dakhni inscriptions are rare, and the one at the Bijapur dargah is the oldest surviving inscription in the language that needs to be taken care of by the government.

Inferences:

I: The government will introduce new plans for preserving the Dakhni inscriptions at Bijapur dargah.

II: Dakhni is a newly emerging language.
questions.solution:
The statement mentions the need for the government to take care of the Dakhni inscriptions.

But there is no mention of the actions planned by the government in this direction.

Therefore, inference I does not follow from the given statement.

At the same time, the phrase "oldest surviving inscription" in the statement emphasizes the fact that this Dakhni language is an ancient language.

Therefore, Inference II contradicts the given statement.

Therefore, inference II does not follow.

Hence, none of the inferences follow.
